newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Konka sees H1 output up 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: China's Konka sees H1 output up 20 pct.

text.p: Chinese television maker Konka Group Co Ltd expects output to rise more than 20 percent in the first half of 1997 over the same period in 1996, a company official said on Thursday.
The output increase was likely to generate a similar year-on-year rise in the Shenzhen-based company's first-half sales, the official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
He declined to give exact figures or an estimate of profits.
Konka posted net profits of 142.7 million yuan on 2.0 billion yuan turnover for the first six months of 1996.
Shenzhen-listed companies must publish their 1997 interim results by August 30.
Konka, China's second biggest television maker, posted a net profit of 346 million yuan for the whole of 1996, up 29 percent from 268 million yuan in 1995 under international accounting standards.
On Thursday, Konka said the Bank of China (BOC) had agreed to lend it 3.8 billion yuan to fund business expansion.
It gave no other details on the loan and company officials declined to give further details.
Trading in Konka's A and B shares was suspended on Thursday morning on the announcement, and would resume in the afternoon, the Shenzhen Stock Exchange said in a notice.
On Wednesday, Konka's A shares closed at 30.1 yuan, while its B shares ended at HK$10.65.
